world.title: Intellectual Property and Traditional Medicine: Rethinking Access, Benefit Sharing and Data Governance - World Health Organization (WHO)
world.summary: Recent developments in the international intellectual property landscape—including the WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge, ongoing IGC negotiations, and broader discussions on access and benefit sharing and digital governance—highlight the need to examine their implications for traditional medicine. As traditional medicine knowledge becomes increasingly digitized and utilized through research, artificial intelligence and innovation ecosystems, new policy questions arise regarding equitable benefit sharing, governance of traditional medicine data, and the recognition of Indigenous Peoples and local communities as rights holders in the stewardship and governance of their knowledge systems. This side event aims to facilitate dialogue on these emerging issues and identify considerations for future international cooperation.Register to watch online.

daily_top5.title: Intellectual Property and Traditional Medicine: Rethinking Access, Benefit Sharing and Data Governance - World Health Organization (WHO)
daily_top5.summary: Recent developments in the international intellectual property landscape—including the WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge, ongoing IGC negotiations, and broader discussions on access and benefit sharing and digital governance—highlight the need to examine their implications for traditional medicine. As traditional medicine knowledge becomes increasingly digitized and utilized through research, artificial intelligence and innovation ecosystems, new policy questions arise regarding equitable benefit sharing, governance of traditional medicine data, and the recognition of Indigenous Peoples and local communities as rights holders in the stewardship and governance of their knowledge systems. This side event aims to facilitate dialogue on these emerging issues and identify considerations for future international cooperation.Register to watch online.

daily_top5.title: WHO launches new primary health care course to strengthen health systems globally - World Health Organization (WHO)
daily_top5.summary: Health is a human right – yet not everyone can access the health services they need, when and where they need them, without financial hardship. Primary health care (PHC) provides a whole-of-society approach to achieving universal health coverage, putting people and communities at the centre of health systems. Despite nearly 50 years of global commitment to PHC, implementation remains fragmented.

daily_top5.title: WHO Health Emergencies EPI-WIN webinar: from framework to action: operationalizing emergency ready primary health care for community protection and resilient health systems - World Health Organization (WHO)
daily_top5.summary: Health emergencies—including disease outbreaks, pandemics, climate-related events, humanitarian crises, and natural disasters—are increasing in frequency and complexity. As the first point of contact for most populations, primary health care (PHC) plays a critical role in engaging communities, detecting health threats early, protecting communities and health workers, maintaining essential health services, and supporting rapid emergency response.
